elaine (Design): quick one — attaching the new credential management modal iteration. two things we want feedback on: 1) keyboard/focus order when creating vs rotating a key, 2) the severity/wording of the revoke warning. cc @sam for a11y, @kevin for implementation constraints kevin (Eng): looks cleaner. question: do we keep the focus inside the modal after rotation success? right now we re-route to list view which steals focus. could be fine but might break screen reader flow sam (A11y): prefer staying in-modal until user dismisses. screen reader users lose context when DOM replaces modal with list. also the revoke warning has low contrast on the icon, and the "Irreversible" word doesn't get announced as an alert unless aria-live or role=alert used. omar (PM): from product POV we want people back on the list quickly after rotation so they can copy the new secret. but agree keyboard users should not lose context. maybe we auto-focus the new secret input inside the modal and provide a clear "done" CTA that returns to list when activated elaine (Design): proposed compromise: keep them in-modal, focus on the new key input (select all), add a dismiss button "Done — return to keys". for revoke path, show stronger color on the icon, and change copy to: "This key will be permanently revoked. Any services using it will stop working immediately." less jargon. kevin (Eng): implementation notes: selecting input on open is trivial. keeping in-modal is also simple. to announce revoke as an alert: we can add
or set aria-live="assertive" on the warning. caution: some browsers will re-read entire modal if we change focus abruptly. sam (A11y): code suggestion for revoke alert: ```
This key will be permanently revoked. Any services using it will stop working immediately.
``` also: ensure the warning icon has at least 4.5:1 contrast if used as standalone info. if it's decorative, add aria-hidden=true and rely on text. omar (PM): what about scoping permissions? design currently shows a dropdown "Key role: read / write / admin". can we surface a brief tooltip that explains implications? non-tech users keep choosing admin by mistake elaine (Design): yep — proposed microcopy under the dropdown: "Admin can manage apps and rotate keys — choose only when necessary." hover tooltip + a short help link. keep the tooltip accessible: keyboard focusable and ESC to dismiss. kevin (Eng): tiny nit: tooltip should not trap keyboard focus; it should be reachable by keyboard but not steal focus. we can use aria-describedby on the dropdown to point to the tooltip content when visible. sam (A11y): confirm keyboard flow: Tab to dropdown, press ? to open tooltip (we can also add a small info button next to dropdown that's keyboard focusable). avoid relying only on hover. elaine (Design): thanks — i'll update the mock: stronger icon contrast, assertive alert for revoke, modal stays open after rotate with selected input + Done CTA, accessible tooltip next to role dropdown. will push PR for copy changes tomorrow. :thumbsup: deploy-bot: build/test pipeline succeeded for branch feature/keys-modal-a11y (artifact 2026-08-12T09:13Z) omar (PM): thanks team. can we schedule a brief review once the PR is up? 15 min sync after lunch works for me kevin (Eng): works for me sam (A11y): works — i'll prep a short checklist (contrast, aria-live, focus order, tooltip keyboard target). elaine (Design): added meeting invite. i'll include the updated screens and a short diff of copy changes.
